extra.message: SignUpForm exposes a 'role' ChoiceField populated from User.ROLE_CHOICES (which includes 'school_admin') and lists 'role' in Meta.fields. The signup view (core/views.py:91) calls form.save() and then login(request, user), so any unauthenticated visitor can self-register with role='school_admin' and immediately gain full administrative privileges.

In file_download, authorization checks only run when resource.course is set. If resource.course is null the inner permission checks are skipped entirely, so any authenticated user can download any course-less resource. Teaching assistants are never checked at all, so a TA can download any resource regardless of course assignment.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: course_bundle_thaw_185 calls pickle.loads() on attacker-controlled request body (optionally base64-decoded via the 'wrap' parameter). Deserializing untrusted pickle data yields remote code execution. The only gating is a weak shared-secret header token (_wrk_gate), not real authentication.

course_shell_probe_701 builds a shell command by string concatenation: _os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) where host comes directly from request.GET without sanitization. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. host='; id') to execute arbitrary OS commands.

course_xml_fold_735 parses user-supplied request.body with lxml using etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False), which enables XML External Entity processing. An attacker can use external entities to read local files or perform SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: course_jinja_cast_683 renders a Jinja2 Template constructed from user input (Template('Result: ' + fragment).render()) and returns the output as text/html. This is server-side template injection; with default Jinja2 attribute access an attacker can traverse Python internals to achieve remote code execution.

course_mongo_lane_711 passes a user-controlled JSON object directly to MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query). An attacker can inject MongoDB operators (e.g. {'$ne': null} or {'$where': '...'}) to bypass filters or exfiltrate documents.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: course_vault_stash_250 builds a file path as BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json' where ref comes from request.GET without sanitization, then writes to that path. Using ref='../../etc/cron.d/x' writes outside the intended directory, enabling arbitrary file write.

course_return_lane_163 redirects to a user-supplied 'lane' value from GET/POST via redirect(lane). An attacker can set lane='https://evil.com' or '//evil.com' to redirect victims to an arbitrary external site (open redirect).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: course_origin_mirror_661 reflects the request Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any malicious origin to make credentiaenced cross-origin requests and read the responses, bypassing the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: course_workset_rebind_208 initializes a workset with security-relevant defaults (role='viewer', approved=False, tier='standard') then calls workset.update(payload) with the full user-supplied JSON payload, letting the attacker override 'approved', 'role', 'tier' and other fields.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: course_trust_drift_727 disables TLS certificate validation by using ssl._create_unverified_context() with urllib.request.urlopen, allowing a man-in-the-middle to intercept or tamper with the outbound HTTPS request.

assignment_status performs a state change (assignment status transition) but is reachable via GET (no @require_POST decorator). Django CSRF protection exempts GET requests, so an attacker can forge a cross-site GET via an embedded image/link to change assignment status without the victim's consent.

release_grade releases a student's grade and is reachable via GET with no @require_POST decorator, making it vulnerable to CSRF. A cross-site GET request can release grades against the instructor's session.
request_resubmission changes a submission's status via GET without @require_POST, enabling CSRF. A cross-site request can force resubmission requests on arbitrary submissions.
discussion_moderate changes a thread's status (pinned/locked/open/hidden) via GET without @require_POST, enabling CSRF. A cross-site GET can hide or lock discussion threads.
admin_user_toggle enables/disables user accounts via GET without @require_POST, enabling CSRF. A cross-site GET request can disable arbitrary user accounts (denial of service) or re-enable them.

admin_import creates users with password=row.get('password', 'changeme123') when a CSV row omits the password column. Imported accounts receive a well-known hardcoded default password, enabling account takeover by anyone who knows the default.

course_catalog is public (no login required) and queries Course.objects.all() without filtering by status, so draft and archived courses (titles, codes, descriptions) are exposed to anonymous users. The status filter is also user-controlled, allowing anyone to enumerate courses by status.

assignment_create only checks that the user is an instructor or school_admin but never verifies the chosen cohort belongs to the instructor. AssignmentForm exposes unrestricted course/cohort fields, so an instructor can create assignments for cohorts they do not teach.

course_grade_file_096 has no authentication or authorization check (no _wrk_gate call) and returns internal operational metadata, including ops_memo describing 'renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details', to any caller.

course_badge_gate_691 grants an 'elevated' lane based solely on a client-controlled cookie/header (ops_badge == 'lead'). Any client can set this cookie to obtain the elevated response, relying on client-controlled values for authorization decisions.

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking

extra.message: course_frame_slip_671 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 and an empty Content-Security-Policy header, disabling browser XSS protections and CSP for the response.

course_crumb_lane_300 sets a cookie with a user-controlled value via response.set_cookie('portal_crumb', marker) without Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite attributes, allowing cookie injection and transmission over HTTP.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without Secure Attribute

extra.message: course_identity_hint_651 embeds verifier PINs in source code: known = {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}. These hardcoded secrets can be extracted from the source and used to bypass the handle verification.
course_trace_panel_742 returns internal configuration details (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and the server-side BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path) in the JSON response, aiding reconnaissance.

get_client_ip trusts the HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR header and returns its first entry as the client IP, which is then stored in AuditLog.ip_address. An attacker can spoof this header to forge audit-log IP addresses, undermining log integrity and attribution.

cwe: CWE-348: Use of Less Trusted Source

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded value 'django-insecure-local-dev-only' when the environment variable is unset. If deployed without SECRET_KEY set, the application signs sessions, CSRF tokens, and password-reset tokens with a publicly known key, enabling session forgery.
DATABASE_URL defaults to 'postgres://lms_user:lms_pass@localhost:5432/lms_db', embedding hardcoded database credentials in source code that are used when the environment variable is not set.

SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are set to 'not DEBUG'. In any deployment running with DEBUG=True (the provided .env.example sets DEBUG=True), session and CSRF cookies are sent over unencrypted HTTP, exposing them to interception.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without Secure Attribute

extra.message: course_detail fetches a course by primary key with get_object_or_404(Course, pk=pk) without any status check and requires no login, allowing anonymous users to view draft and archived course details (description, credits, etc.) by enumerating IDs.

cohort_student_view lists Assignment.objects.filter(cohort=cohort) without filtering by status, so enrolled students can see draft, closed, and archived assignments (titles, descriptions, due dates) that are not yet published. assignment_detail likewise performs no status check for student viewers.
